record.title: Epoch AI revises its Abilene estimate to 1,019k H100e
record.summary: Epoch AI’s Nov 1, 2026 update raised its estimated current compute for the OpenAI Stargate Abilene site from 764k to 1,019k H100-equivalents, and its estimated IT power from 618 MW to 824 MW. Epoch says it combines satellite imagery, cooling-equipment power modeling, company disclosures, regulatory filings and drone imagery. Its profile estimates buildings 7–8 operational by analogy to earlier buildout timing, while noting Oracle had not given a date for those final buildings. The revised figures are an independent model estimate, not metered IT load or independently confirmed delivery of the final buildings.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Epoch AI’s dated Nov 1, 2026 update revised its published Abilene site estimate to 1,019k H100-equivalents and 824 MW IT power, from previously listed estimates of 764k H100-equivalents and 618 MW. This establishes a change in Epoch’s estimate, not the site’s measured live capacity.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Epoch’s site profile identifies the campus as operational and estimates buildings 7–8 operational by Nov 1 based on analogy with prior building delivery timing; the profile states Oracle had not supplied a delivery date for the final two buildings.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed sources do not establish metered IT load, the exact number or type of chips currently energized, or direct Oracle confirmation that buildings 7–8 were delivered and operational by Nov 1.

evidence_gaps.description: No dated Oracle or utility record confirming delivery and energization of Abilene buildings 7–8 was inspected.
The reviewed sources provide modeled compute and IT-power estimates, not measured facility load or independently confirmed active chip count.

brief.importance_rationale: If directionally accurate, a roughly one-third revision to estimated compute at a major AI campus affects capacity and power expectations across a large AI infrastructure project; the rating reflects possible consequence, not verification of the estimate.
limitations: The 1,019k H100e, 824 MW, $31.2B and 302.4k B300 figures are Epoch AI estimates, not independently measured capacity or cost.
Epoch estimates buildings 7–8 operational by analogy to earlier buildout timing; it states Oracle has not given a date for the final two buildings.
No metered IT load, utilization, or independent facility audit was found in this review.

relationships.summary: OpenAI and Oracle separately announced Vera Rubin OCI availability and a planned multi-gigawatt expansion on Oct. 27; that announcement does not verify the Abilene estimate or building 7–8 delivery.

other.title: NVIDIA and Oracle announce Vera Rubin OCI availability and a planned multi-gigawatt expansion
other.summary: NVIDIA and Oracle announced that Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs are generally available on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), alongside plans to expand OCI Superclusters with Rubin systems to multi-gigawatt scale. The release frames GPUs as serving model training and inference and CPUs as handling agent tool execution, code execution and retrieval between model calls. Oracle and NVIDIA describe customers as able to scale CPU and GPU resources independently, but the announcement supplies no measured utilization, customer cost or matched end-to-end agent workload results. Oracle describes OpenAI as exploring Vera CPU use in early access and quotes OpenAI as saying it is bringing Vera into production; these company statements do not establish delivered fleet scale or measured effects.
